Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal count of freeze–thaw transition days, based on PRISM daily data (1991–2020), aggegated to NHD+ catchments,
Notes: Captures thermally transitional zones; relevant for soil structure, infiltration disruption, and freeze–thaw runoff events.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of 95th percentile of daily precip on wet days, based on PRISM daily normals (1991–2020), aggegated to NHD+ catchments
Notes: Captures storm severity at the upper tail. Correlated with flash flood potential and runoff generation efficiency.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median number of wet days (≥ 0.1 mm/day) per season, based on PRISM daily normals (1991–2020), aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Describes storm frequency and seasonal spacing. Interacts with intensity to shape hydrograph form and flood likelihood.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median percent cover by dominant NLCD class aggegated to NHD+ catchments
Notes: Proportion of catchment covered by dominant land cover class. Useful for integrating land cover with slope, aspect, and flow.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Normalized Shannon–Weiner Diversity Index of NLCD land cover classes, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures local land cover heterogeneity. Useful for modeling transitions or mosaic patterns in mixed-use catchments.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median elevation range (max − min elevation), based on 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Reflects terrain steepness (catchment relief). Indicates potential energy for runoff, erosion risk, and hydrograph flashiness.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of the cosine of aspect, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: North–south slope orientation. +1 = north-facing. Linked to solar exposure, snow persistence, and evapotranspiration.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of the sine of aspect, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: East–west slope orientation. +1 = east-facing. Influences early-day sun exposure, melt timing, and phenology.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: IQR of combined curvature types, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Reflects variation in concavity/convexity across catchment. High values = complex terrain, mixed flow paths, and erosion potential.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of planform (horizontal) curvature, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Detects flow convergence/divergence on hillslopes. Negative values indicate channels; positive values indicate ridges. Useful for identifying channel initiation, ponding, and routing divergence.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of profile (vertical) curvature, derived from 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Captures slope acceleration/deceleration along flow paths. Distinguishes concave (depositional) from convex (erosional) zones.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Watershed elongation ratio, calculated from catchment geometry, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Catchment elongation index. High elongation = quicker runoff and flashier peaks; low elongation = slower, more spread-out hydrograph.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Watershed circularity ratio, calculated from catchment geometry, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Watershed compactness (circularity). High values = more synchronous flow and steeper hydrograph; low values = delayed runoff and flatter hydrograph.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of stream length per catchment area, derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Total stream length per unit area. Higher values indicate more dissected basins and faster hydrologic response.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of average flow path length, derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Average stream path length. Longer paths = slower response; shorter paths = more rapid runoff concentration.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Zonal median of stream slope (elevation drop per unit flow length), derived from NHD+ data.
Notes: Slope of main stream path. Controls runoff velocity and hydrograph steepness.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~1–5 sq-km (catchment-level)
Description: Relief ratio (elevation range divided by stream length), based on 10 m NED data, aggregated to NHD+ catchments.
Notes: Ratio of elevation range to main channel length. Indicates basin steepness and hydrologic energy. Higher values = flashier, more erosive flow.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Dominant Köppen-Geiger climate class, aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Provides broad-scale climate context (e.g., humid continental vs. semi-arid). Useful for regional stratification.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Count of unique USDA Plant Hardiness Zones, aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Reflects cold tolerance diversity; transitional zones may affect vegetation, snowmelt timing, and freeze–thaw processes.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Dominant USDA Plant Hardiness Zone, aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Captures dominant cold tolerance regime based on minimum winter temperatures. Relevant for snowmelt timing and freeze–thaw sensitivity.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Fraction of cropland (NLCD), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Indicates anthropogenic land use in agricultural regions. Associated with increased runoff, reduced infiltration, and higher ET demand.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Fraction of forested land (NLCD), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Forest cover enhances interception and storage. Typically reduces peak flows and lowers skew.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Fraction of grassland (NLCD), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Moderates evapotranspiration and infiltration rates; especially important in mixed rangeland systems.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Fraction of urban land (NLCD), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Urban development increases imperviousness; strongly associated with peak flow generation and positive flood skew.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Mean slope (from NED), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Captures large-scale terrain steepness; useful for distinguishing dissected uplands from broad flatlands.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Median slope (from NED), aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Central tendency of slope; more robust to extreme values than the mean. Useful for assessing runoff dominance.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (macroregional zone level)
Description: Mean elevation of gage locations, aggregated to custom macroregional zones
Notes: Captures broad elevational gradients that influence temperature, snow persistence, and hydrologic timing.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of annual mean temperature from PRISM 1991–2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Governs evapotranspiration, freeze–thaw, and snowpack formation. Represents the baseline thermal regime.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of total annual precipitation from PRISM 1991–2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents typical annual moisture supply; important for soil moisture availability, runoff potential, and vegetation productivity.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal mean of the percentage of annual precipitation falling May–August from PRISM 1991–2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Characterizes warm-season water input. Useful for identifying storm-driven systems tied to convective seasonality.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of the percentage of annual precipitation falling May–August from PRISM 1991–2020 climatological normals, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures the typical proportion of precipitation falling in the warm season—important for Great Plains hydrology.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of annual NDVI amplitude for 2016 from MODIS data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates the magnitude of seasonal greenness change. Reflects vigor and seasonality of vegetation response to climate.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of the interquartile range (IQR) of NDVI values for 2016 from MODIS data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Measures seasonal variability in greenness. IQR is robust to outliers, making it effective in mosaic or transitional landscapes.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of the length of the 2016 growing season (NDVI-based), aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents the number of growing-season days. Useful for modeling evapotranspiration and baseflow duration.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median of the seasonal peak NDVI in 2016 from MODIS, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures maximum greenness during the growing season. Proxy for peak biomass or vegetative productivity.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal mean of 10 m NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects average terrain steepness across ecoregions. Linked to stream energy, flow velocity, and sediment transport.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal skewness of 10 m NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Asymmetry of slope distribution. Highlights dominant gentle or steep terrains; useful for detecting terrain breaks.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal standard deviation (SD) of slope values from 10 m NED data, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures terrain variability including extremes. May indicate complex topography or abrupt slope transitions.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal interquartile range (IQR) of 10 m NED slope values, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Captures slope diversity in a robust way, less sensitive to outliers. Linked to flow complexity and infiltration.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil (0–5 cm) composed of clay particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects soil infiltration potential — higher clay content typically leads to greater runoff generation and flashier flood responses.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil (0–5 cm) composed of silt particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Represents intermediate soil texture, balancing infiltration and runoff potential.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal modal fraction of surface soil (0–5 cm) composed of sand particles from SSURGO2, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects soil drainage capacity — higher sand content is associated with greater infiltration and slower runoff response.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal median (typical) stream order within the stream network, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects typical stream network scale — useful for understanding catchment structure and routing dynamics.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~50,000–100,000 sq-km (Level II) based size and heterogeneity
Description: Zonal maximum stream order in the network, aggregated to Level II ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects maximum stream network scale — provides context on floodplain extent and drainage complexity.

Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)
Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: used as a spatial predictor

Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)
Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Useful for capturing east-west climatic or physiographic gradients (moisture availability, storm type).

Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)
Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Useful for capturing broad climatic gradients (e.g., temperature, seasonality).

Effective Analytical Resolution: Point-defined (gage-level metadata)
Description: Point-based (gage-level) metadata used as a station-level predictors, not derived from zonal aggregation.
Notes: Influences temperature regime, snow persistence, and climatic classification.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Standard deviation of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures variability across seasons. Sensitive to outliers—useful for detecting flashiness or hydrologic irregularity.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: IQR (25th–75th percentile) of seasonal precip totals from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Seasonality spread (middle 50%). Robust alternative to StDev for characterizing intra-annual precipitation variability.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Sum of zonal medians of fall monthly precip totals (Sep–Nov) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Fall recharge, baseflow resetting; marks transition from convective to frontal systems.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Sum of zonal medians of winter monthly precip (Dec–Feb) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Indicates snowpack formation potential and winter water storage.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Sum of zonal medians of spring monthly precip (Mar–May) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures convective storm seasonality (flood-prone regions).

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Sum of zonal medians of summer monthly precip (Jun–Aug) from PRISM 1991–2020 normals aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Key springtime recharge and flood generation season; relevant to melt-transition systems and early crop needs.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal median of percent cover of dominant land class (cropland, forest, etc.) from MODIS 2016 land coveraggegated to Level III ecoregions
Notes: Represents the dominant cover type. More interpretable than nominal class. Useful in mosaicked or fragmented landscapes.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Normalized Shannon-Weiner Diversity Index of MODIS land classes aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Captures land use fragmentation, heterogeneity. May correlate with infiltration variation and complex runoff behavior.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal median of surface roughness, derived from 10 m NED, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Small-scale terrain heterogeneity. Linked to microrelief, runoff dispersion, ponding, and infiltration zones.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal mean ofTopographic Wetness Index (TWI) values, derived from 10 m NED data, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Average soil moisture tendency. Combines slope and upslope contributing area.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal mode of 10 m NED Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) values aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Most common soil moisture potential class in catchment. Helps classify dominant runoff tendency.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal assignment  of ordinal NED Topographic Wetness Index (TWI) classes, derived from 10 m NED, aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Categorical version of TWI to simplify terrain–moisture interactions. Improves model interpretability.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal median of STATSGO2 permeability values aggegated to Level III ecoregions
Notes: Rate at which water infiltrates soil. Low permeability = high runoff potential = more positive skew.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal modal soil hydrologic group (A–D) from STATSGO2 aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: USDA hydrologic group (A = high infiltration, D = high runoff). Linked to storm response class.

Effective Analytical Resolution: ~5,000–50,000 sq-km (Level III) based on ecoregion size and similarity
Description: Zonal median of 10 m NED flow accumulation (upslope contributing area) aggegated to Level III ecoregions.
Notes: Reflects wetness accumulation potential and flooding propensity at catchment scale.
